headline: Solar Power Hits 3 Terawatts—with Acceleration That Defies Expectations
meta_description: The world has reached 3 terawatts of solar capacity. The speed of deployment is accelerating dramatically—a sign of renewable energy's growing momentum.
summary_short: The world has achieved 3 terawatts of installed solar power. What's remarkable: the second and third terawatts took far less time to build than the first.
body:
The world has reached 3 terawatts of installed solar power capacity. What makes this milestone genuinely striking is not the number itself, but the speed at which it arrived.

The journey to the first terawatt took a full decade after solar crossed the 100-gigawatt threshold in 2012. But the second and third terawatts—doubling the capacity again—were deployed in less than five years combined. That acceleration reveals a quiet transformation: solar has moved from niche technology to industrial-scale infrastructure, with costs falling and deployment networks maturing year on year.

The data tells a story of momentum. Each successive terawatt comes faster than the last, suggesting the renewable energy transition is not just underway, but gathering pace. For a world racing against climate deadlines, that trajectory matters.
quick_facts: World solar capacity has reached 3 terawatts total
First terawatt took 10 years after the 2012 100-gigawatt milestone
Second and third terawatts deployed in under 5 years combined
Solar deployment is accelerating, not slowing
